applicabilityBasis.summary: Monetrix documents base USDM as a 1:1 USDC mint and redemption token, while strategy yield is separated into sUSDM. That makes USDM an apparent payment-stablecoin product, although no public GENIUS issuer pathway is identified.

genius.notes: Monetrix's public material documents USDM mechanics but does not identify a permitted payment stablecoin issuer, state-qualified issuer, official GENIUS application, or foreign-issuer registration. The base USDM token is separated from the yield-bearing sUSDM wrapper, so it remains in the apparent-payment-stablecoin review rather than being treated as a savings wrapper. The apparent product classification is retained, but documented 1:1 USDC exits do not establish a statutory obligation to redeem national currency or bank-deposit money; GENIUS excludes another fixed-value digital asset from monetary value. The exact legal issuing/contracting entity and domicile were not identified in the reviewed .xyz documentation and are omitted. Same-name monetrix.io on-ramp entities are not joined to this token without evidence. The public 1:1 USDC redemption policy has a three-day cooldown, adjustable by governance. The live issuer collateral API is self-reported and explicitly marks the reserve view unreconciled; disclosure presence does not establish eligible reserves or solvency. No monthly independent or issuer reserve-attestation series was located. No public GENIUS enforcement action was found in reviewed sources/searches. The issuer framework remains pre-effective and the broad DASP prohibition begins July 18, 2028; no present illegality is inferred from missing public authorization.

negativeEvidenceReview.summary: No public GENIUS approval, official application, state-qualified authorization, or foreign-issuer registration naming Monetrix or USDM was located. Monetrix documentation supports the payment-stablecoin-like product classification but does not announce a GENIUS pathway.
